Prospective per-quarter flux-closure gate |predicted/observed SAP flux - 1| <= 0.2
Per-quarter reviewed noise: robust out-of-transit scale and red-noise beta (Pont et al. 2006; Winn et al. 2008)
Probability exposure integration 20/40/80 chosen per case before FPP
Stock TRICERATOPS priors; no contrast curve or MOLUSC
Field-wide ephemeris rule: a low-order (1:1, 2:1, 1:2) DR25 TCE/KOI match on another star leaves the candidate unresolved (post_boi/ephemeris.py; Coughlin et al. 2014)
not_restored: PRF wings beyond the calibrated footprint
Custom companion priors or composite-flux conditioning
MOLUSC/RUWE companion limits (uncalibrated for G 16-19; Wood et al. 2021; Penoyre et al. 2022)
limitations: TRICERATOPS thresholds come from TESS data; Giacalone et al. 2021 report unreliable FPP below SNR 15 (IV.1)
The known-object calibration ran on KOIs that skipped the survey detector and vetting
The upstream 2.2-arcsec unresolved radius assumes Gaia completeness that faint hosts lack
TRICERATOPS cannot model optical-ghost, crosstalk or other ephemeris-match contamination
Brown dwarfs are not modeled, so for Jupiter-sized bodies the planet scenario includes brown-dwarf companions of the same radius

First V3 native fit: eccentricity 0.98 [0.95, 0.99] with the transit near apoastron and periastron inside the star in 88% of samples; the stellar density prior is essentially unconstrained (4274 +/- 37709 kg/m3). Its 4.87-h duration and ±4.4-h model wings left 728 cadences outside the ±3.22-h protection. The circular-equivalent density (~100 kg/m3) points to an evolved host. A duration-aware second generation was started and stopped (cases/2130965547378157568-g2/stopped.json). Under the EXOFASTv2 collision boundary (native-rule-amendments-20261025.json), 88% of samples are excluded and the retained weight ESS is 575 < 1000; the physical subset is a grazing (b 0.94), 6.3-h transit.

post_boi.native stopped at its geometry check: 311 of 12,736 posterior samples (2.4%) have no defined transit duration, all at a/R* 1.00-1.06. The fit needs stellar density 19 kg/m3 [14, 27] against the catalogue prior 1683 +/- 2192 kg/m3, so the transit is far too long for a dwarf host: a giant host or a blend. Radius ratio 0.066 [0.061, 0.074], b 0.47, in 3 closure-passing quarters.

First V3 fit: 14.7 h duration (supplied 3.84 h), 193 model cadences outside protection; post_boi.protection transfer 29-38% of transit amplitude (6.4-9.3 formal sigma) for three physical samples. 99.75% of posterior samples cross the EXOFASTv2 collision boundary (median e 0.988); the 62 physical samples have e 0.83-0.91. A separate duration/clock-aware generation (-g2: supplied duration 0.600 d, trend window 6.0 d, measured protection mask) is queued; the first fit is preserved.

First V3 fit: 8.9 h duration (supplied 3.36 h), e 0.69-0.89, 98.9% of samples beyond the EXOFASTv2 collision boundary, 161 model cadences outside protection; post_boi.protection transfer 30-47% of amplitude (4.8-9.2 formal sigma). Like the 8.83-day sibling, the fit prefers a much lower host density than the K-dwarf prior: possibly another host or wrong stellar parameters. Separate -g2 generation queued; first fit preserved.
Bimodal radius ratio k 0.053/0.066/0.674 (16/50/84%), b up to 1.58: small planet versus grazing body; quantile SNR 0.21 < 3. Only quarters 2, 4 and 16 pass flux closure.
